explanation: Keep the lowest earlier price and the best profit found so far. Each price can be the selling day; a zero profit represents making no trade.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n prices. One scan updates the minimum price and best profit in constant time per day.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Only low and best are retained.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Java algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The running minimum is the cheapest price seen before or at the current selling day. Buying at that minimum maximizes profit for this selling day, and the stored best covers all processed selling days. Starting best at zero permits no transaction when every sale would lose money.
walkthrough: For prices [8,3,7,2,9], price 7 gives profit 4 after buying at 3. A later price 2 becomes the new minimum; selling at 9 then gives profit 7. Return 7.
edgeCases: The purchase must precede the sale.
A decreasing price sequence returns zero.
A one-day sequence permits no profitable trade.
